summary.text: Lupe Castillo, a Republican who has worked as a chef and in the pharmacy industry, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the open U.S. House seat in Illinois's 4th District to Patty Garcia.
According to Ballotpedia, she was born in San Antonio, Texas, and she ran for the Illinois House in 2022 and for this congressional seat in 2024.

paragraphs.text: Castillo was born in San Antonio, Texas. In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey she describes herself as a second-generation American whose first language was Spanish, and says she began working as a child on newspaper routes.

She attended a Catholic high school, working for four years to help pay tuition, and earned an associate degree from Washburne Community Trade School in 2000. Her career experience includes work as a chef and in food service, retail and the pharmacy industry.

Castillo says she has been a member of the Chicago Alternative Policing Strategy (CAPS) and the 10th District Advisory Committee of the Chicago Police Department; Ballotpedia lists affiliations with Southwest Side GOP, Chicago GOP and the Little Village Community Council. The Sun-Times reports she has lived in the district for 43 years.

She ran as the Republican candidate for Illinois House District 23 in 2022 and lost to Edgar Gonzalez Jr., 82.0% to 18.0%. In 2024 she ran for Illinois' 4th Congressional District and lost to Jesus Garcia, 27.3% to 67.5%.
Castillo was unopposed in the March 17, 2026 Republican primary for the open seat.
During the campaign, she said she was running on "pro-family values and policies."
She received 16.1% of the vote to Patty Garcia's 71.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.

sources.title: What to know about the 4th Congressional District race to replace U.S. Rep. Jesus 'Chuy' Garcia
